name: Lightning AI

modes.label: The one free Default CPU Studio (4 cores / 16 GB)
modes.commit_note: Only one free CPU Studio can be active per account at a time. On the Free plan the free Studio has a 4 h session limit, after which it converts to a paid Studio (billed from credits) unless restarted; disabling auto-sleep also converts it to paid. On Pro and above the session limit is unlimited.
modes.note: Pricing page CPU tab: Default (CPU) 4 cores / 16 GB 'Free', free hours 'unlimited'. Valid only for a concurrency of 1.

modes.label: On-demand CPU Studio (fixed shapes)
modes.note: Per-second billing from credits (1 credit = $1). The on-demand price of an additional Default 4/16 Studio (beyond the free one) is not published, so it is omitted: 4-core workloads fall through to Large 8/32. Plan max CPUs per Studio: Free 32, Pro 64, Teams 96/192. Auto-sleep after 10 min idle (idle tail billed; sleeping Studio costs $0).

modes.label: Interruptible CPU Studio
modes.commit_note: Interruptible: the machine can be reclaimed. Data prep (32c) and Data prep max (64c) have no interruptible price.

modes.label: GPU Studio, on-demand (1-GPU rates)
modes.note: Price per GPU-hour with the host CPU/RAM bundled (the CPU/RAM shape per GPU machine is not published, so vcpu_h/ram_gib_h = 0). The per-GPU rate differs on 2/4/8-GPU shapes: e.g. 8-GPU A100 80GB is $1.55/GPU, 8-GPU A100 40GB $3.87, 8-GPU L40S $4.21, 8-GPU B200 $9.86. Free plan: 1 GPU per Studio, 2 concurrent GPUs, 4 h A100/H100/H200 session limit.

modes.label: GPU Studio, interruptible (midpoint of live band)
modes.commit_note: Interruptible; the price is a live band that moves intraday.
modes.note: Midpoint of the 1-GPU interruptible bands on lightning.ai/pricing 2026-09-28 (T4 0.58-0.69, L4 0.73-0.87, RTX PRO 6000 3.38-4.06, A100 80GB 3.66-4.39, H200 3.82-4.58). H100, L40S and A100 40GB have NO interruptible price ("-"), so an H100 request falls back to the H200 band. For T4, RTX PRO 6000 and A100 80GB the whole band is above on-demand.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: One-time up to 30 credits (5 on sign-up + 25 with a card). Paid CPU Studios are pay-as-you-go credits; concurrency of paid CPU Studios on Free is not published (null). Max 32 CPUs per Studio. When credits run out, workloads are gracefully shut down (no overage). GPU limits are on "Free (GPU)"; the free-Studio 4 h restart is on "Free (free Studio)".

plans.name: Pro (monthly)
plans.note: $50/mo includes 40 credits/mo ($10 pure fee). Credits expire 12 months after issue, so unused ones roll over within the year. 4 GPUs per Studio; 6 concurrent GPUs; 200 GB Drive; no free-Studio restarts.

plans.name: Pro (annual)
plans.note: $240/yr prepaid (shown as $20/mo) includes 240 annual credits, so the fee is fully credit. Flagged 'sales' only because it is a 1-year commitment (self-serve checkout).

plans.name: Pro (academic, annual)
plans.note: Academic toggle: $10/mo billed annually, 100 annual credits (= $8.33/mo). Academic eligibility required; 1-year commitment.

plans.name: Teams (monthly, per user)
plans.note: $140/user/mo includes 50 credits/user/mo. Plan card says '96 core CPU', comparison table says 192 max CPUs per Studio (largest shape is 96 cores anyway). 8 GPUs per Studio; 12 concurrent GPUs; 2 TB Drive; spending limits; credit auto-reload; AWS Marketplace billing.

plans.name: Teams (annual, per user)
plans.note: $119/user/mo billed annually, 600 annual credits per user (= 50/mo). 1-year commitment.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom credits at bulk pricing; use your own AWS/GCP credits; VPC/BYOC and on-prem; full-node B200; unlimited concurrent GPUs; 99.95% SLA; SAML/SSO; bring your own images. Reserved clusters are quote-only.

plans.name: Free (free Studio)
plans.note: The one free Default CPU Studio on the Free plan has a 4 h session limit; per the compare-table tooltip it converts to a paid Studio after reaching the limit (hero footnote: 'require restart every 4 hours'). Auto-sleep docs: a free Studio also converts to paid if auto-sleep is disabled. Paid Studios on Free have no published session limit.

plans.name: Free (GPU)
plans.note: GPU Studios on Free: max concurrent GPUs 2; A100/H100/H200 sessions limited to 4 h (T4/L4/L40S unlimited); 1 GPU per Studio. One-time up to 30 credits (see free.one_time_credit). Paid CPU/GPU usage is pay-as-you-go credits. The free Default Studio restarts every 4 h. A100/H100/H200 sessions are limited to 4 h; 1 GPU per Studio; 2 concurrent GPUs; 50 GB Drive cap. When credits run out, workloads are gracefully shut down (no overage).

plans.name: Pro (monthly) (GPU)
plans.note: GPU Studios on Pro (monthly): max concurrent GPUs 6. $50/mo includes 40 credits/mo ($10 pure fee). Credits expire 12 months after issue, so unused ones roll over within the year. 4 GPUs per Studio; 6 concurrent GPUs; 200 GB Drive; no free-Studio restarts.

plans.name: Pro (annual) (GPU)
plans.note: GPU Studios on Pro (annual): max concurrent GPUs 6. $240/yr prepaid (shown as $20/mo) includes 240 annual credits, so the fee is fully credit. Flagged 'sales' only because it is a 1-year commitment (self-serve checkout).

plans.name: Pro (academic, annual) (GPU)
plans.note: GPU Studios on Pro (academic, annual): max concurrent GPUs 6. Academic toggle: $10/mo billed annually, 100 annual credits (= $8.33/mo). Academic eligibility required; 1-year commitment.

plans.name: Teams (monthly, per user) (GPU)
plans.note: GPU Studios on Teams (monthly, per user): max concurrent GPUs 12. $140/user/mo includes 50 credits/user/mo. Plan card says '96 core CPU', comparison table says 192 max CPUs per Studio (largest shape is 96 cores anyway). 8 GPUs per Studio; 12 concurrent GPUs; 2 TB Drive; spending limits; credit auto-reload; AWS Marketplace billing.

plans.name: Teams (annual, per user) (GPU)
plans.note: GPU Studios on Teams (annual, per user): max concurrent GPUs 12. $119/user/mo billed annually, 600 annual credits per user (= 50/mo). 1-year commitment.

plans.name: Enterprise (GPU)
plans.note: GPU Studios on Enterprise: max concurrent GPUs unlimited (Enterprise). Custom credits at bulk pricing; use your own AWS/GCP credits; VPC/BYOC and on-prem; full-node B200; unlimited concurrent GPUs; 99.95% SLA; SAML/SSO; bring your own images. Reserved clusters are quote-only.

perf_source: ComputeSDK benchmarks (benchmarks.json): cold-start TTI median 2026-08-07, burst TTI median at 100 concurrency 2026-08-21, DAX total 2026-08-14 (8 logical CPUs / 38.75 GiB x86_64 env). Measured the Lightning Sandbox API, whose price is unpublished. Later runs (2026-09-10) failed.
caveats: The Sandbox API (cpu-1 1/1 GB, cpu-2 2/8, cpu-4 4/16, cpu-8 8/32, cpu-16 16/64) has NO published price. The card prices Studio shapes. cpu-4/8/16 match the Default/Large/X-Large Studios, but whether Studio rates apply is unverified.
No on-demand price is published for a second Default 4/16 CPU Studio (only 'Free' for one). The engine therefore puts 4-core on-demand workloads on Large 8/32 ($0.51/h), which may overestimate.

GPU Studio prices are per GPU with host CPU/RAM bundled. The per-GPU rate varies by 1/2/4/8-GPU shape (e.g. A100 80GB $2.71 single vs $1.55 on 8-GPU; A100 40GB $2.19 single vs $3.87 on 8-GPU); only 1-GPU rates are encoded (B200 is listed for 8-GPU nodes only at $9.86/GPU).
Interruptible GPU bands are live and move intraday; on T4, RTX PRO 6000 and A100 80GB they sit above on-demand. TPU Studios ($3.03-$4.72/TPU-h) are not encoded.
10 GB free storage is account-wide (Drive), not per sandbox; above it $0.10/GB-month billed daily. Drive caps: Free 50 GB, Pro 200 GB, Teams 2 TB. Snapshot storage price not separately published.
When credits run out, Lightning warns and then gracefully shuts down all Studios: there is no overage. Credits (free and paid) expire after 12 months, so monthly plan credits roll over within a year.
Free plan concurrency for paid CPU Studios is not published. GPU concurrency: Free 2, Pro 6, Teams 12.
Egress, ingress and public IPv4 pricing not published. Regions are not listed as geographies; compute runs on AWS, GCP, Lightning (Voltage Park), Lambda, Nebius, NScale and Voltage.
Auto-sleep after 10 min idle (customisable on paid tiers), so up to 10 min idle tail is billed per session. A sleeping Studio costs $0 compute.

2026-09-21 reprice (third-party usagepricing.com): GPU rates moved and the Free tier went from 15 monthly credits to a one-time up-to-30 grant. usagepricing lists H100 at $4.50, but the official page shows $4.68 (2026-09-28).
Annual plans are flagged 'sales' only because they are 1-year prepaid commitments; they are self-serve.
Studio start/wake time is not published, so no boot overhead is modelled; Studios are dev environments, not an instant sandbox API.

Multi-GPU per-GPU rates (live 2026-09-29): 2-GPU L4 $1.19, RTX PRO 6000 $2.82, A100 40GB $2.19, A100 80GB $2.69, H100 $4.68, H200 $4.50; 4-GPU T4 $0.88, L4 $1.20, L40S $2.97, RTX PRO 6000 $2.79, A100 40GB $2.19, A100 80GB $2.68, H100 $4.68, H200 $4.50. Multi-GPU interruptible bands are sometimes far below 1-GPU: 4-GPU T4 $0.29-0.35, 4-GPU L40S $1.90-2.28, 8-GPU L40S $2.80-3.36, 8-GPU A100 40GB $2.57-3.08 per GPU (no 1-GPU spot for L40S / A100 40GB).

Starting a Studio from a custom launch image ('Bring your own images') is Enterprise-only; lower tiers customise the persistent environment interactively (Docker is installed inside Studios). The Sandbox API separately accepts a user OCI image.

Other storage tiers: high-performance volumes on Lightning Cloud $0.30/GiB-month; AWS EFS $0.0125/GB-day + $0.0375/GB read + $0.075/GB write; GCP Filestore $0.5625/GB-month (EFS/Filestore Enterprise-only per compare table). The 10 GB free is per account and storage is billed while Studios sleep.
Max concurrent GPUs (Free 2 / Pro 6 / Teams 12) counts GPUs across Studios, Batch Jobs, multi-machine training and Deployments together.

fleet.verification: Phone/identity verification; work or university email verifies faster. No card required for free signup; support can expedite verification.
fleet.tiers: Free up to 2 concurrent GPUs; Pro 6; Teams 12; Enterprise unlimited by contract.
fleet.notes: One free Studio is an included allowance, not proven total account concurrent-CPU-instance cap. GPU counts from rendered pricing; verification may take 2–3 business days for personal emails, not a quota-increase SLA. Country eligibility applies.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Stop a sandbox. For a persistent sandbox the control plane captures an auto-snapshot and returns its id; the sandbox id keeps resolving and can be brought back with [`start`](#start).
snapshot_auto.note: Sandbox API with persistent=True: stop() auto-snapshots the filesystem (not running processes) and resume() restores it (sandbox.md: 'Sandboxes auto-save state on stop and resume right where you left off'). Whether the create-time timeout auto-stop also auto-snapshots is not stated. Studios: auto-sleep after 10 min idle keeps the home dir/system packages on persistent storage (that is persistent_disk, not a memory checkpoint; Docker images not persisted).

snapshot_on_demand.note: sandbox.snapshot() / `lightning sandbox snapshot create` on a running sandbox, optional TTL and excludes; new sandboxes boot from it via Sandbox.create(snapshot_id=...) / `create --snapshot-id`. Filesystem only, no memory. Snapshots do not carry the network policy (restore defaults to allow-all). Studios can also be duplicated (fork).

harness_api.quote: Use the Lightning Sandbox Python SDK to create ephemeral sandboxes, run commands, manage files, capture snapshots, and open interactive PTY sessions from Python.
harness_api.note: SDK/CLI surface is commands, files, PTY, snapshots, network policy only; no Claude Code/Codex/agent-session API anywhere in the docs manifest. The Agents page is a tutorial for writing your own LitAI agent in a Studio and scheduling it.

egress_allowlist.quote: Egress firewall, set at create time only — no runtime mutation.
egress_allowlist.note: Sandbox API network_policy: allow-all (default), deny-all, or NetworkPolicy(allow_cidrs=[...]) default-deny. Docs: 'enforcement is IP-based'; blocked connections are dropped and logged. Cannot be changed after create; snapshot restore defaults back to allow-all unless re-specified. No documented egress control for Studios (Enterprise BYOC/VPC only).

egress_http_rules.quote: A single `NetworkPolicy` models every mode (mirrors Vercel's `NetworkPolicy`):
egress_http_rules.note: The only modes are allow-all, deny-all and a CIDR allowlist; no host, method, path or header rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Restrict access to your endpoint by enabling security. There are 2 ways of securing an endpoint in the API builder.
ingress_rules.note: Studios: public URLs opened per port via API builder / Port viewer plugins, with optional token or basic auth. Sandbox API: `ports=` chooses which ports are opened but the SDK returns no public URL ('Reach the port from inside the sandbox or another box on the same network'). No IP allowlists documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets are encrypted and served securely as environment variables in studios at runtime.
secret_proxy.note: User/teamspace secrets are injected as env vars into Studios; the Sandbox API has only image_secret_ref for private registry pulls. No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: The Drive can also hold high-performance volumes: fixed-size volumes that Lightning AI provisions on Lightning Cloud and mounts read/write at `/teamspace/lightning_storage/<volume name>`.
volume_attach.note: Studios/Jobs: high-performance volumes ($0.30/GiB-month) tied to one compute location/region, resizable up only; also EFS/Filestore cloud folders (Enterprise) and S3/GCS data connections. Sandbox API only has a storage_gb writable-disk override; Drive/volume mounts for sandboxes are not documented.

volume_shared.quote: All Studios in a teamspace share the same drive. This means any Studio can access the files of the other Studios.
volume_shared.note: Teamspace Drive is a shared read-write filesystem across Studios, Jobs, Deployments; cloud folders 'any workflow, Studio, or cluster can mount'. Applies to Studios, not documented for Sandbox API.
